findings: In fiscal year 2018, Hewlett Packard Enterprise officially ceased selling custom-designed commodity servers to Tier 1 service providers, which the company defined as Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Apple, Tencent, and Baidu, in order to pivot toward selling higher-margin products.
The company reported a $1.2 billion artificial intelligence infrastructure order from cloud service provider Vultr to supply its data center computing systems.

The rating rests on the company's strategic pivot away from manufacturing commodity hardware for top-tier hyperscalers, focusing instead on higher-margin data center contracts with Tier 2 cloud providers.

findings: Hewlett Packard Enterprise reported research and development expenditures of $2.5 billion for the fiscal year ended October 31, 2025, which represents approximately 7% of its total net revenue of $34.3 billion, according to the company's annual report on Form 10-K.

The company reported a record financial performance for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 with a revenue increase of 34% year-over-year to $12.2 billion, driven by surging demand for AI infrastructure and its acquisition of Juniper Networks.
The rating rests on the company's multi-billion dollar annual innovation budget and robust double-digit quarterly revenue growth fueled by the integration of its newly acquired networking business.
